valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS viewed at the 12-month target date of November 2027, anchored to FY2026 guidance of $5.37-$5.59 and ~670.5M diluted shares)

bear.driver: Persistent energy and haulage cost inflation, sluggish residential construction, and slower Arcosa integration
bear.assumption: FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS $5.60 at 15.0x P/E

base.driver: High-single-digit aggregates pricing, partial margin recovery, full-year Arcosa contribution, and buyback accretion
base.assumption: FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS $6.20 at 18.0x P/E

bull.driver: Stronger North American infrastructure and residential volume recovery, faster Velocity cost savings, and multiple expansion
bull.assumption: FY2027 adjusted diluted EPS $6.70 at 20.5x P/E

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS of $6.20, the $93.16 close implies 15.0x forward P/E.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $6.20 (6.7 pp of price return).
valuation.watch_metric: North American aggregates pricing and Adjusted EBITDA margin (23.5% in Q3 2026) alongside Arcosa integration contribution
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4 and FY2026 earnings release (expected February 17, 2027)

analyst_notes: Following CRH's Q3 2026 release on October 29, 2026 (which trimmed FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $7.8B-$8.0B on cost inflation and soft residential demand), Truist ($120) and Citigroup ($108) nudged targets higher on November 2 while DA Davidson trimmed to $114. All five tracked analysts maintain Buy-equivalent ratings with targets ranging from $108 to $135, broadly aligned with our $111.60 base case (+19.8% upside) as the market looks past near-term cost headwinds toward 2027 margin recovery and the $8.5B Arcosa acquisition.
